At Espumilla Beach, you may find yourself listening to the surf and wandering along the sand. The beach lies beside James Bay on Santiago Island. Mangroves and palo santo trees grow beyond the sandy strip, and a walk here combines open ocean views with patches of island vegetation.

This shore is important to sea turtles, which use it for nesting. The sand bears traces of their activity, even though few turtles may be seen during a daytime visit. Brightly coloured crabs and coastal birds appear near the rocks. It is especially absorbing to watch a heron standing perfectly still as it waits for prey, then striking with a precise movement.

A trail leading inland introduces the island's dry vegetation and small birds. Some local pools change with the seasons, so each visit offers different observations. Espumilla suits travellers who enjoy alternating between the shoreline and a path among the trees. It is a lovely place to stop after a short walk and catch another glimpse of the ocean through the mangroves.

## Estelí – Nicaragua's archaeological centre!

Estelí is a city situated near the border between Nicaragua and Honduras and is a centre of agribusiness, specialising in premium cigars.

## Estelí – activities for visitors!

Among the main attractions for visitors are the many archaeological sites surrounding the city. In an area known as Las Pintas, ancient rock paintings, fossils and remains of giant mammals that lived here more than 20,000–30,000 years ago have been discovered. Picturesque hills and mountains surround the city, and the popular La Estanzuela Waterfall is not far from Estelí. This relatively small waterfall plunges 40 metres into a pool of crystal-clear water. Swimming enthusiasts may be disappointed, however: the water is very cold. The many hotels and restaurants are known for excellent service, and some restaurants may even offer you a complimentary cigar after lunch.

Fazenda Florença appears in the itinerary as a coffee plantation operating since 1852. The visit explores the estate's history and coffee cultivation.

This stop is combined with visits to other estates in the Coffee Valley. Such a route offers a chance to see several historic properties and learn about the development of coffee production in the region.
